digest.component_or_area: git write policy checker (raw git writes gate)
key_entities: primitive set: add commit commit_tree read_tree rm_cached update_ref write_tree
propositions: The existing git write policy checker (d37e) enforces mechanism rules (no raw subprocess git) but misses protocol violations where git-adapter mutation primitives are composed outside atomic transactions, as proven by reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 staging and committing without a lock.

R3 rule adds seam-composition enforcement by binding receiver references to git_adapter module (import or dynamic-loader forms) and firing on mutation-primitive calls (add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree) from outside three sanctioned seam files (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py).

Two out-of-seam composition sites require durable reasoned inline markers, not remediation: reconcile_helpers.py's binding-store snapshot (selective staging boundary blocks seam reroute) and __main__.py's detached-index lock purge (CAS-protected, never touches main index).

R3 receiver binding resolves no false positives across src/ and scripts/ (set.add, session.commit, read-only git_adapter exports remain silent), verified by --report dry-run and regression test parametrization on lookalike filenames under different packages.

Module-size ratchet violation from the _purge_committed_reconciler_locks reasoned marker is resolved by extracting the pass-lock lifecycle cluster (lock steal, legacy lock purge, lock acquire) into _pass_lock_lifecycle.py, keeping marker intact and seam-composition rule still applied within the new module.
Budget registry update for relocated REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_STEAL config-read marker and seam-clean proof verification ensure no read-via marker escapes the gate by relocation.
